text:
Okay, listen! You know how I’m totally scared of the big slide at the park? Like, my knees get all wobbly and my tummy feels like it’s full of butterflies having a party. Well, yesterday, my best friend Leo was super brave because he’d been on it before. He said, "Come on!" so I grabbed his hand tight-tight.

I didn’t actually have *my* courage. I borrowed his! It was like wearing his superhero cape even though it wasn’t mine. When we got to the top, I almost cried, but Leo squeezed my hand. So I went whoosh down. And guess what? I didn’t die! I laughed! My heart stopped beating fast and started doing happy dances.

When we got to the bottom, Leo said, "See? You did it!" But I shook my head. "No, *we* did it." He said, "Doesn't matter whose hand you held. You still went down the slide." 

That’s when I realized something huge. If you borrow someone’s bravery to do the scary thing, it still counts as *your* win. Because you’re the one who slid! So next time, if you’re scared, just grab a friend’s hand. Borrow their spark. It’s okay! The courage becomes yours while you’re using it, and then maybe you’ll keep some forever.
